title: Higher direct images commute with bounded-below filtered colimits
statement:
Let $f\colon X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] that is quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. Let $\mathcal R$ be a sheaf of rings on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and let $(K_i^\bullet)$ be a filtered diagram [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] of complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of $\mathcal R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ vanishing
below a fixed degree $a$. Then for every $q$ the canonical map
$\varinjlim_iR^qf_*K_i^\bullet\to R^qf_*(\varinjlim_iK_i^\bullet)$, with $f_*$ as in [det-pe-topos-functoriality-inverse-image] and $R f_*$ as in [def-sfb-right-derived-functor], is an isomorphism of
sheaves on $Y_{\mathrm{proét}}$.

proof.text: Fix $q$ and, for every complex $L$ vanishing below $a$, put $P_L(V)=H^q(X\times_YV,L)$ as an abelian presheaf. The base-change functor on pro-etale sites and the direct image on underlying sheaves are those of [det-pe-topos-functoriality-inverse-image]. Apply [lem-pe-bounded-complex-direct-image-presheaf] to obtain $P_L^\#\cong R^qf_*L$, naturally in $L$. Here direct image has coefficients in $f_*\mathcal R$, and all comparisons below are read as abelian sheaves, so no assumption that $\mathcal R$ is pulled back from $Y$ is needed.

Let $V$ be an affine object of $Y_{\mathrm{proét}}$. It is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. By [det-pe-topos-functoriality-inverse-image], $U=X\times_YV$ is an object of $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$. The map $U\to V$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by part (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], applied to the given $f$. Part (2) of the same node, with $V$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated, shows that $U$ itself is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

Form the termwise colimit $K=\varinjlim_iK_i$ of module sheaves; its terms below $a$ are zero since those diagrams are identically zero. Module-sheaf colimits exist and their underlying abelian sheaves are the abelian-sheaf colimits by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. Functoriality gives a presheaf map $\varphi:\varinjlim_iP_{K_i}\to P_K$, with the colimit here taken sectionwise in abelian groups. On an affine $V$, Step 2 permits applying [det-pe-bounded-continuity-sections] to $U=X\times_YV$ and the original diagram on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$. Its comparison is exactly $\varphi(V)$; it is an isomorphism. There is no substitution of evaluation of a sheaf colimit for a sectionwise colimit in this argument.

source.place: Second paragraph, comparison on affine objects

proof.text: Every object $V$ of $Y_{\mathrm{proét}}$ has a covering by affine objects $V_j$ by [det-pe-wcb-cover]. If two sections of the source of $\varphi(V)$ have equal images, their restrictions to each $V_j$ are equal because $\varphi(V_j)$ is injective. Every target section restricts to a section on $V_j$ which lifts because $\varphi(V_j)$ is surjective. Thus $\varphi$ is locally injective and locally surjective in the precise sense of [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-iso-locally-bijective], so $\varphi^\#$ is an isomorphism. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact] with the constant ring $\mathbf Z$ to these abelian presheaves: sheafification preserves colimits, hence $(\varinjlim_iP_{K_i})^\#\cong\varinjlim_iP_{K_i}^\#$. The natural identifications in Step 1 turn $\varphi^\#$ into the map of the statement: on each colimit cocone leg it is the map induced by $K_i\to K$. This proves that the canonical comparison is an isomorphism.

source.place: Second paragraph, affine covers and sheafification
